The item stays DELTA/partial because of three clauses that this re-check did not re-examine: the leading radial estimate of (5.42), the radial half of (5.44), and the endpoint extensions for the stress and the error. The sharp member of (5.43) is no longer one of the reasons. No declaration states the edge-weighted stress error at rate q^{2h}, but the clause follows from stated declarations by combination alone: firstCutoff_finite_bound (BaseResidual.lean:1727) and slowSum_zero_leading_finite_bound (:1702) state C q^(2*h) for the n = 1 cutoff factor and for the ζ-quotient sum of the terms n ≥ 2, slowSum_split_first (:1753) is the exact splitting, and the proof of weighted_slowSum_bound (:1815-1873) combines them by the stated product and sum bounds to reach B q^(2*h) ζ δ^{-N} before its final weakening at lines 1874-1877. The same one-step proofs carry this to the final base, whose schedule admissibility is stated (FinalSlowBase.scales_spec, FinalSlowBase.lean:245). I read these proofs and did not compile the derived statement. The earlier reason for medium, that p. 107 needs the sharp member, was an arithmetic slip: with Σ − Σ^(0) = ε (Q/q)^{A+1/2} (T̂ − T_0) the q^h member already gives M_2 and hence the printed 2 − κ_s, and the Lean states exactly that class from its q^h bound (BaseStressClasses.higherStress_meanClass, BaseStressClasses.lean:491). On the radial estimate, the exterior identities, (5.44), the endpoint clause and the error-flatness encoding the earlier adjudication stands unchanged.

findings.summary: (5.43) asserts two bounds, C_I q^{2h} ζδ^{-N} and the weaker C_I q^h ζδ^{-N}. Every declaration that states the edge-weighted stress error states the q^h member only; the sharp rate is stated at the two ingredient lemmas (first cutoff factor, and the ζ-quotient sum of the terms n ≥ 2), and the q^{2h} member follows from them by repeating the stated proof of BaseResidual.weighted_slowSum_bound without its last weakening step (about 60 lines; read, not compiled).

The third estimate of (5.42), identifying the leading radial profile, was not found stated. The Lean has uniform boundedness of q^{1/2}u_{r,B} with nothing subtracted, and a q^h envelope for q^A u_{r,B}.

(5.44)'s first clause, u_B = u^{(0)} as a full velocity identity on I_mean, was not found stated. The Lean mean-interval theorem gives the swirl formula and vanishing axial sum, saying nothing about the radial/stream component.
The endpoint clause is stated for u_B and p_B only. No declaration was found giving continuous extension of the fixed derivatives of the stress τ_phys or the error ℰ_B to η = ±1.

Several clauses of the proposition are faithfully stated, but outside the omnibus theorem: (5.42)'s first, second and fourth estimates, the exterior identities at X ≥ X_+, the endpoint extensions, and the unrestricted error flatness.

The paper's 'for every fixed X_max, uniformly on [0,X_max]×[-1,1], |∂^α ℰ_B| ≤ C q^M' is encoded as flatness along filters with compact carrier and q → 0, and inside exists_final_base only for approaches of bounded similarity radius.
